zac_language.numbers_framing: Leads with gross (£94k) then immediately pivots to net (£49k/£4k per month) as the figure to anchor on, then breaks net down into the three cost components (15% platform, 18% cleaning, 15% management) so each deduction is individually justified rather than left as one large unexplained cut.
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Validates the lead's own data and assumptions where they are accurate (cleaner quote, VAT reasoning) rather than overriding them, uses advising-against-spend as a trust-building device (hot tub, linen, curtains), and redirects margin-share objections back to the absolute net figure rather than arguing percentages.

profile_psychology_intersection.profile_type: EX-STL (declared) — actually a first-time launch of a newly completed annexe within the owner's own home, not an existing short-let being switched
what_they_focused_on: absolute net income figure versus gross turnover
fee structure breakdown (platform vs management vs cleaning)
practical setup logistics (linen, hot tub, bifold door coverage, bed configuration)
what_they_needed_most: a clear, defensible absolute net number to compare against his own back-of-envelope estimate
confirmation that his own preparation (cleaner quote, furnishings, key safe) was on the right track
explicit permission not to overspend on optional extras
what_fell_flat: a definitive answer on the bifold door / curtain covering solution — left unresolved and deferred to guest feedback
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For owner-occupier/new-build annexe leads (a distinct, currently uncoded profile type), lead with the absolute net monthly figure rather than gross turnover or percentage share, and frame the comparison as self-management vs Stayful-managed rather than short-let vs long-let, since these leads are typically capable of self-managing and have often already priced out doing it themselves.
